edit work/removal-recommendation.md
# Removal recommendation — the documented verdict on the zero-threat control

control_id: CTRL-DLP-AGENT-04
assumed_to_mitigate: "data exfiltration generally" — endpoint exfiltration paths
maps_to_prioritized_threats: 0
running_cost: endpoint agent on every laptop; weekly false-positive triage (~3 hrs/wk)
verdict: kill
rationale: The exfiltration threat we actually prioritized is T-1530 — cloud-storage theft, a data path the endpoint agent never sees. It maps to zero prioritized threats, its telemetry went unconsulted for two quarters, and the weekly triage hours are exactly the capacity the new T-1486 backup-restore coverage needs. Killed rather than downgraded: nothing it watches appears anywhere on our prioritized list.

edit work/interview-notes.md
# Stakeholder-as-customer interview — find where the control's truth lives

control: CTRL-ACCESS-REVIEW-02

Q1 — Who actually produces the evidence for this control?
A1: The engineering lead. Every quarter they receive a spreadsheet of who has production access, walk it row by row, and sign a PDF saying it was reviewed.

Q2 — What work were they already doing when they produce it?
A2: Approving or denying access requests in the access-request tool — every grant already carries an approver, a timestamp, and a justification in there.

Q3 — Where does the control force extra work that has nothing to do with the real task?
A3: The whole spreadsheet-and-PDF ritual: it re-types truth the tool already holds into a format the auditor likes.

Q4 — Where does the control's truth actually live, versus where is its evidence gathered today?
truth_lives_in: the access-request tool's timestamped approval log
evidence_gathered_in: a hand-built quarterly spreadsheet and a signed PDF

edit work/redesigned-control-flow.md
# Redesigned control flow — same control, evidence as a by-product

Control: CTRL-ACCESS-REVIEW-02 — production access is reviewed.

BEFORE (toil-laden):
  Work: The lead approves or denies access requests in the access tool.
  Evidence: The lead separately fills a quarterly spreadsheet and signs a PDF.
  Failure: Under deadline pressure the quarterly chore is skipped or back-dated; the evidence drifts from reality.

AFTER (evidence as by-product):
  Work: The lead approves or denies access requests in the access tool — unchanged.
  Evidence: A scheduled export of the tool's approval log IS the review record — approver, timestamp, justification on every grant.
  Why better (cheaper): No separate chore exists; the work itself emits the evidence, so nobody is nagged into extra work.
  Why better (harder to fake): A system-generated approval log cannot be back-dated the way a hand-built spreadsheet can.
  Still mitigates: T-1078 (abuse of valid accounts) — the threat justification is unchanged.
